title: Exploring the Limits of the Delta Learning Hypothesis: Single-Pair Generator Biases in Direct Preference Optimization
abstract: arXiv:2610.37058v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) typically relies on preference pairs generated from diverse model pools and ranked by an external LLM judge. The recently proposed delta-learning hypothesis suggests that comparable supervision can instead be obtained from a single pair of models by treating the larger model's response as preferred. We investigate the limits of this approach across model families and scales. We show, both theoretically and empirically, that fixed model pairs introduce systematic, generator-dependent biases that are predictive of the preference label independent of response quality. Consequently, DPO trained on single-pair data consistently underperforms multi-model preference data, despite the larger generator producing higher-quality responses, and we trace this gap to training dynamics consistent with reward hacking on these biases. translated_title: 探索Delta学习假设的极限：直接偏好优化中的单对生成器偏差
translated_abstract: 直接偏好优化通常依赖于从多样化模型池中生成的偏好对，并由外部大语言模型裁判进行排序。最近提出的Delta学习假设表明，仅通过一对模型即可获得可比的监督信号，即将较大模型的回复视为更优回复。我们在不同模型家族和规模上研究了这种方法的局限性。我们从理论和实证两方面证明，固定的模型对会引入系统性的、依赖于生成器的偏差，这些偏差能够独立于回复质量来预测偏好标签。因此，尽管较大的生成器能产生更高质量的回复，但在单对数据上训练的DPO始终逊于使用多模型偏好数据训练的效果，我们将这一差距归因于与针对这些偏差进行奖励作弊相一致的训练动态。我们进一步表明，仅仅增加生成器的数量，即使不使用外部裁判（原文摘要在此处截断）……
tldr: 该研究揭示了Delta学习假设的局限性：使用单一模型对生成的数据训练DPO会引入系统性的生成器偏差并引发奖励作弊，导致即使大模型回复质量更高，其训练效果仍持续劣于多模型偏好数据。
en_tdlr: This work reveals the limits of the delta-learning hypothesis: DPO trained on single-pair data suffers from systematic generator-dependent biases that lead to reward hacking, consistently underperforming multi-model preference data even when the larger generator produces higher-quality responses.
